facts.fact: TechCabal reports Nigeria's National Digital Addressing System (NDAPS), led by NIPOST, launched on October 1 with 11-character alphanumeric digital postcodes.

NGA.note: Only a CBN data-location directive is mentioned; no licensing, switch or PAPSS fact.

facts.fact: TechCabal says Communications Minister Bosun Tijani released the National Digital Cloud Policy in August 2026, with NITDA's supporting cloud guidelines.
NIPOST says the policy directs federal agencies to meet cloud hosting needs through the government's shared services model, with Galaxy Backbone as provider.
NIPOST says its core postcode database is hosted and managed by Galaxy Backbone, an arrangement it bases on the National Digital Cloud Policy.

NGA.note: Nothing on digital financial consumer protection.
Galaxy Backbone hosts government data; the document does not say it rents to outside organisations. AWS Local Zone in Lagos is a zone, not a region.

facts.fact: NIPOST says the August 2026 National Digital Cloud Policy's Highly Sensitive (Level 3) tier requires government records to stay within Nigeria with domestic disaster recovery; its Open tier has no residency restriction.
TechCabal says a CBN directive requires banks, fintechs and payment companies to move transactional data from foreign cloud servers to Nigeria by 1 January 2027.

NGA.note: NDPC is only said to be engaged on a DPIA; no appointment or ruling stated.
No statement on the law, regulations or an NDPC decision.
Only a pending DPIA engagement with NDPC; no law, ratification or authority fact.

facts.fact: The August 2026 National Digital Cloud Policy, per TechCabal and NIPOST, classes government data as Open or Highly Sensitive (Level 3), the latter to be kept within Nigeria.
NIPOST says the core NDAPS postcode database and its backups are hosted and managed in Nigeria by government-owned Galaxy Backbone.

NGA.note: Nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: NIPOST says government-owned Galaxy Backbone hosts and manages the core NDAPS postcode database for it.
NIPOST, a federal agency, says its core postcode database is hosted in Nigeria by government-owned Galaxy Backbone.

NGA.note: NIPOST says backups and DR are in Nigeria but names no place, so no distance can be set.
